title: Kimsuky Detection and Exploitation Analysis
content_md: Kimsuky detection depends on recognizing the group’s tradecraft in your own telemetry, not just on matching a hash. Kimsuky is a North Korean APT group, and one of its published campaigns impersonates diplomats to deliver LNK files and PowerShell droppers. Those techniques leave traces in ordinary Windows Security logs: script hosts launched from user-writable folders, hidden PowerShell, new services and scheduled tasks, and quiet account changes. This article covers Kimsuky detection using a log sample analyzed in LogTotal, a log analysis tool that matches events to known threats. Below, we describe where the logs came from, what LogTotal flagged, which findings hold up against the raw events, and what the response should be. Get Started For Free Kimsuky Analysis The tradecraft in this sample reads more clearly against the group’s background and its recent campaigns, so we start there before turning to the logs. Who is Kimsuky Kimsuky is a North Korean state-sponsored APT group focused on intelligence collection. MITRE ATT&CK tracks it as G0094, and vendors also call it APT43, Velvet Chollima, Black Banshee, THALLIUM, Emerald Sleet, TA427, and Springtail. Its activity is believed to align with North Korea’s Reconnaissance General Bureau. CISA assesses that the group has most likely operated since 2012.
